name: The Residual Book - cross-sectional residual momentum, long and short
hypothesis: A crypto book that hedges out the common factor and holds only the residual, sized by cross-sectional momentum of that residual, earns where an unhedged book does not - because the factor is most of what an unhedged crypto book owns, and the residual is where the idiosyncratic information lives. Assembled from published work rather than from our own numbers.
mechanism: Daily bars from the shared 15m catalogue on the screened universe. Causal rolling loading on BTC with a window ending strictly before the day; the residual is r_i - beta*r_B. Every 14 days, rank the cross-section by compounded residual over 28 days (skipping the most recent), long the top third and short the bottom third, size by inverse residual volatility with equal gross per leg, and add the factor leg h = -sum(w*beta). Gross capped at 1.0 on EVERY day. Costs 0.30% round trip plus perpetual funding with the ledger's sign.

helped.what: Enforcing the gross cap on EVERY day rather than only at rebalances
helped.effect: drift had carried gross exposure to 2.67x on a 1.0 cap; fixing it moved total return 400% -> 512%, max drawdown 64.5% -> 48.8%, Sharpe 0.66 -> 0.78 and positive years 5 -> 6 of 9

helped.what: The perpetual funding leg on a sustained short book
helped.effect: the book RECEIVED +26,042 over the research period, confirming the design's weakest claim on our own tape; kill criterion K3 did not fire

helped.what: Hedging the net factor loading with h = -sum(w*beta)
helped.effect: net exposure averaged +0.036 with sd 0.141 against a gross of ~0.90, so the book is close to factor-neutral and K1 did not fire

helped.what: A minimum residual-share floor on the inverse-volatility denominator
helped.effect: removed positions taken in rounding error: a name with no residual to own had been attracting the largest weight in the book

hurt.effect: t = 2.24 against the Harvey-Liu-Zhu bar of t > 3, so the result DOES NOT clear a hurdle that was registered before any code existed
6 of 9 years positive: 2018 -7.4% and 2022 -3.7% lose outright and 2024 +7.6% is far below the bar

hurt.what: Drawdown, which the mandate names as an objective to minimise
hurt.effect: max drawdown 48.8%, which is not close to acceptable

hurt.what: Trading costs at a two-week rebalance
hurt.effect: 122,578 on a 100,000 book across 196 rebalances - the second-largest line in the account despite a horizon chosen to keep turnover down

open: Which factor set the residual is taken against: BTC alone today, against the published CPT3 or DS3. Registered as the first decision of implementation rather than a default, and the first thing to try because it changes what 'idiosyncratic' means.
Whether anyone has TRADED residual momentum on crypto after costs. DS3 shows it prices the cross-section, which is not the same claim.
O5 - non-price inputs (crowd positioning, copy-trading flow, on-chain, attention), deliberately deferred so a second hypothesis is held in reserve.
The 2018 and 2022 losses, both crypto winters: whether a state variable can stand the book aside without becoming another fitted parameter.
rules: A constraint stated in a formula must be enforced on every bar, not at every decision. 'Subject to sum|w| <= L' applied only at rebalances let the book lever itself to 2.67x by holding winners.
Inverse-volatility sizing needs a floor on the denominator: a name with no residual to own attracts the largest position in the book.
Declare the number of trials before reporting a Sharpe. Understating it is the specific lie the six dead systems were built on.
A first run that fails its registered bar is information, not a setback. Sweeping until it passes is exactly what the deflated Sharpe exists to punish.
2026 was not read. The catalogue's lock is structural, not a convention.

results.detail: total return +511.6%, max drawdown 48.8%, Sharpe 0.78, t = 2.24, funding received +26,042, costs 122,578, 196 rebalances, 6 of 9 calendar years positive. DOES NOT clear the registered t > 3 hurdle.

closed_because: The sealed 2026 came in at -26.1% because the cross-sectional ranking inverted, and a 20,000-draw bootstrap of the strategy's own annual distribution gives P(year >= +30%) = 43.9% even in the regime where it works, so the mandate was never reachable.
